description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley values for different linguistic features across three multilingual BERT-based models — mBERT, XLM-R, and chLSTM — as evaluated in the context of morphosyntactic probing. The horizontal axis categorizes linguistic features into groups: L1, L2, T, R1, R2, R3, and R4+, likely representing different syntactic or morphological properties (e.g., L for lexical, T for tense, R for relational features). The vertical axis represents the Shapley value, ranging from 0 to over 80, with major gridlines at intervals of 20, indicating the relative importance or contribution of each feature to the model’s prediction. Each group of bars corresponds to one linguistic feature, with three bars per group representing the three models: mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (light green). The tallest bars appear under the “T” category, where chLSTM reaches a Shapley value above 80, followed closely by mBERT and XLM-R. In contrast, features like L2 and R3 show much lower contributions across all models. The chart is tilted slightly for visual effect, and the legend in the upper right corner clearly identifies each model by color. The overall pattern suggests that the “T” (tense-related) feature is most influential for all models, while other features vary in importance, with chLSTM often showing higher Shapley values than the other two models for most categories.
